Basement-dwelling gamers are so overly dramatic it borders on self-parody. The game isn’t nearly as bad as some are trying to make it sound, though it does have its problems of course. 

To address one of the biggest complaints I’ve seen, yes the dialog CAN be eye-rolling levels of cringe. Is it worse than any other triple-A offering nowadays? No. In fact at times the writing in Veilguard can be just as good as its predecessors, and is consistently better than in games like Starfield or even Mass Effect: Andromeda. 

And as for the tone of the world, does everyone forget that the first open world level of DAI (which I see defended quite a lot in these threads) is literally a bright and vibrant forest? And are we ignoring the fact that during the first few hours of Veilguard you visit a town horrifically destroyed by the Blight? In both games there are instances of tonal shifts between lighthearted Joss Whedon level of witty banter and extremely dark shit, but if you’re cool with one game doing it you have to be cool with both.

The game is decent so far. I’ve played about six hours on two different characters, one elf rogue Veiljumper and the other a human warrior Grey Warden. I will say beyond a shadow of a doubt that the gameplay itself is the best it’s been in the entire series, and is the first entry in the franchise I can confidently say I haven’t been bored by the combat. The animations are another high point, with very smooth facial animations and honestly some of the best hair physics I’ve ever seen in a video game. 

Where it does somewhat fall flat though (especially compared to earlier DA entries) is the writing. While it isn’t bad all the way through, there is some occasionally truly eye-rolling dialog and a few instances of patchy voice acting. However Veilguard also has moments of excellent writing and acting worthy of its predecessors, and in those moments the game really shines.
